| BT-SH-001 | FIXED | CSV formula injection in exported spreadsheet cells | Alpha.11 routes every current report CSV path through one protected structured serializer; focused regression/security coverage is recorded below. |

| BT-SH-002 | FIXED | Pending database-operation marker trusts file paths | Alpha.12 validates the complete marker at its sole Data reader before transition and derives all operative/cleanup locations from trusted configuration; focused hostile-marker and recovery coverage is recorded below. |

| BT-SH-003 | FIXED | Logout does not clear authenticated UserSession | Alpha.13 atomically clears the desktop session before logout audit work and before every new login attempt; focused lifecycle/authorization coverage is recorded below. |

| BT-SH-004 | FIXED | Failed-login lockout update is concurrency-prone | Current login uses database-side atomic increment and conditional lock updates; sequential threshold/audit integration coverage confirms the enforcement path. |

| BT-SH-005 | FIXED | Excel workbook processing lacks hostile-input resource limits | Alpha.20 Batch G enforces file/package/XML/worksheet/row/cell/used-range budgets before disproportionate allocation/traversal, with focused real-workbook and hostile-input coverage. |

| BT-SH-006 | FIXED | Business writes and audit writes are not atomic | Alpha.15 commits affected user/customer/container/business-information state and required audit evidence under one Data-owned transaction, with deterministic audit-failure rollback coverage. |

| BT-SH-008 | FIXED | Username case normalization/uniqueness is inconsistent | Alpha.14 applies one provider-neutral NFKC/lower-invariant comparison identity, stores every new username in a restricted canonical form and relies on the exact database unique index as the concurrent-create arbiter. Legacy canonical collisions fail login closed. |

| BT-SH-011 | FIXED | User listing exposes password hashes and salts via domain entities | BT-ARCH-018 now projects a credential-free immutable administration DTO; reflection/integration coverage excludes hash, salt and failed-login state. |

| BT-SH-012 | FIXED | Persisted batch drafts are not isolated by BinTracker user | Alpha.18 owner-specific schema-4 envelopes carry stable persisted user ID; Services detach on identity change and enforce owner-only Continue/Save/Discard with no name, role or Administrator bypass. |

| BT-SH-013 | FIXED | Malformed draft JSON object graph can crash recovery | Alpha.18 manually validates exact JSON shape, required nested fields, types, identities, enum values, text maxima and checked totals before constructing a recovery graph; invalid evidence is quarantined or retained with a diagnostic. |

| BT-SH-014 | FIXED | Draft JSON read/deserialization is unbounded | Alpha.18 bounds reads to 16 MiB, JSON depth to 8 and line count to 10,000 before/during parsing, rejects rather than truncates and never presents partial state. |

| BT-SH-015 | FIXED | Undefined enum values are accepted at service boundaries | Alpha.16 applies provider-neutral defined-value guards to mutation, report, import/planner and draft-persistence inputs; undefined values fail before branching or writes. |

| BT-SH-016 | FIXED | int quantity/balance arithmetic can overflow | Alpha.16 uses long aggregation and checked conversion/operations across projection, legacy balance, import, correction and report totals; overflow fails closed rather than wrapping. |

| BT-SH-017 | FIXED | Audit-log reads lack service-layer authorization | Every public audit read/review/detail operation now requires a currently revalidated Administrator in Services, including `GetRecentAsync`; anonymous denial is covered. |

| BT-SH-018 | FIXED | Report/read services rely on UI for authentication | Operational reports, customer/container/business/balance reads, correction previews, PDF/export workflows and developer reads now authorize in Services; authenticated Viewer/Operator read access is preserved. |

| BT-SH-019 | FIXED | Session authorization is cached and not revalidated after account changes | Desktop workflow authorization reloads the stable user ID from storage and applies missing/inactive/locked/password-change/role state before each Services boundary; invalid authority signs out and database failure propagates closed. |

| BT-SH-020 | FIXED | Duplicate import prevention is check-then-insert | Import hashes content and the database now owns unique `SourceSha256`; duplicate-save translation plus exact-source retry tests prove the arbiter. |

| BT-SH-022 | FIXED | Authentication checks are inconsistent across services | `ICurrentAccountAuthorization` is the shared client-neutral Services policy for authenticated, operational and Administrator workflows; the public service sweep and focused denial/regression coverage prove consistent enforcement. |

| BT-SH-027 | FIXED | SQLite backup connection string interpolates user-selected filename | Alpha.19 constructs the backup target connection with `SqliteConnectionStringBuilder`; delimiter/quote/Unicode round-trip and real hostile-valid-path tests prove the selected file remains the target. |

| BT-SH-028 | FIXED | Authentication inputs lack strict upper bounds | Login rejects username input over 100 UTF-16 code units and passwords over 256 before database or PBKDF2 work; new usernames are 3-64 and every password creation/reset/hash path shares the 256 limit. |

| BT-SH-030 | FIXED | Authentication availability depends on separate audit writes | Alpha.15 commits failed-login/lock and successful-login state with required audit evidence atomically; audit persistence failure rolls state back and propagates as infrastructure failure before session publication. |

| BT-SH-032 | FIXED | Administrator self-reset can leave session/database state inconsistent | A self-reset persists the replacement credential/`MustChangePassword`, then always ends the desktop session even if the separate audit append fails; the next use requires authentication and credential change. |

| BT-SH-033 | FIXED | Backup source/destination same-file detection is path-string based | Alpha.19 resolves existing directories and uses Windows volume/file identity for source, existing destination, temporary and published files; direct, hard-link and reparse aliases cannot target the source. |

| BT-SH-034 | FIXED | Backup destination overwrite policy is unsafe/ambiguous | Data now enforces unconditional no-overwrite publication. Existing or concurrently created destinations are retained, and a unique same-directory temporary snapshot is moved only into an absent name. |

| BT-SH-035 | FIXED | Database settings writes are non-atomic | Settings and every pending-operation marker publication use flushed unique sibling files, a stable cross-process lease and atomic same-directory move/replace; failed/concurrent writes retain complete prior evidence. |

| BT-SH-036 | FIXED | Batch-draft temporary filename is predictable | Alpha.18 uses create-new GUID temporary siblings, durable flush and an exclusive cross-instance publication lease; it cleans only its own temp and preserves the previous published draft on failure. |

| BT-SH-037 | FIXED | Corrupt-draft quarantine filenames can collide/overwrite evidence | Alpha.18 combines high-resolution UTC and GUID quarantine identity with `overwrite: false`; existing evidence is preserved and a failed quarantine truthfully reports that the source remains. |

| BT-SH-038 | FIXED | EF string lengths are not consistently enforced by SQLite constraints | Schema18 translates mapped maxima into exact SQLite `CHECK` constraints using a deterministic UTF-16 code-unit function; direct oversize writes fail, including supplementary-character boundaries and nullable fields. |

| BT-SH-039 | FIXED | Customer input validation lacks consistent maxima/normalization | Alpha.16 centralizes customer/container maxima in Core, reuses them in Services and EF metadata, and rejects oversize master data before persistence/audit. |

| BT-SH-040 | FIXED | Security identifiers permit Unicode confusables | Authentication usernames retain alpha.14's canonical restricted-ASCII policy. Alpha.16 explicitly classifies customer/container codes as Unicode operational identifiers and preserves established trim/uppercase behavior without compatibility normalization, transliteration or retained-data rewrite. |

| BT-SH-041 | FIXED | Import fingerprinting does not eliminate file-use races | WinForms reads once into `ImportSourceDocument.Content`; analysis/preflight/execution hash and consume those same bytes, so later path changes cannot alter execution input. |

| BT-SH-043 | FIXED | ApplicationSettings singleton invariant lacks database enforcement | Schema18 constrains every settings row to ID 1; the PK plus this `CHECK` prevents invalid/additional settings authorities while preserving normal ID-1 creation and updates. |

| BT-SH-044 | FIXED | Unknown report-filter enums silently return empty data | Alpha.16 rejects undefined Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Movement History, Outstanding and Audit review filters at the provider-neutral service boundary. |

| BT-SH-047 | FIXED | Builds are not reproducible/pinned/locked | Alpha.21 pins supported SDK 10.0.403, commits every project lock graph and requires locked restore in governed build/package security checks. |

| BT-SH-048 | FIXED | No automated dependency/security supply-chain gate | Alpha.21 performs a machine-readable direct/transitive NuGet vulnerability scan and fails closed when advisories are found or configured sources/advisory data are unavailable. The first real scan found GHSA-2m69-gcr7-jv3q and the candidate pins the compatible fixed SQLite native package line. |

| BT-SH-049 | FIXED | Packaged artifacts lack checksum/signing integrity | Alpha.21 emits and rereads an external SHA-256 manifest, then rehashes the validated ZIP. The checksum supplies integrity only; publisher signing remains an explicit external release decision. |

| BT-SH-050 | FIXED | Audit-BinTracker is governance-heavy and lacks code-security checks | Alpha.21 enables the SDK recommended security-category analyzers as errors and makes a Release analyzer build part of the governed security gate without replacing the requirements/source audit. |
